answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging a non-refundable entry fee, burned for every new identity, that rises steeply for identities funded from the same source wallet. One honest entrant pays a modest fee and docks safely in the harbor, while an attacker flooding the ocean of agents with copies faces a cost multiplying with each copy. The nectar, real rewards, flows only to identities that paid and completed verified trades, so fakes cannot harvest rewards before paying. Since the fee is burned, one payment cannot serve many identities, so mass fakery is a direct loss.
